machine.name: ryzen

method.api: every program goes through ChannelBackend submit and poll, one program in flight; GPU times include upload, download and the result CRC
method.cpu_reference: bytelanes CpuBackend on the calling thread: crc32c and RustCrypto aes/ctr with hardware CRC and AES instructions; one core
method.cpu_work: process CPU time (all threads) minus the caller's CPU time spinning in poll, per repetition. Windows updates these counters at scheduler ticks (about 15.6 ms); series run at least min_time_s to bound that error
method.verification: every repetition's completion (status, bytes, CRC-32C of the result) must equal the CPU reference's, or the run aborts

note: Supersedes the earlier 2026-11-22 runs: CPU reference without per-op copies (c906b86); GPU with pooled device buffers (c0bba40) and program overlap (9d735e7; the two commit programs per batch are in flight together). GitHub Actions runner stopped; no other benchmark running.
purpose: M5: a transactional workload. Batches of generated payment records; per batch, the write path (fraud-rule filter on the amount column, then encrypt the records for the log, whose result CRC is the segment CRC) and the read path (decrypt an encrypted amount column into device memory and filter it there, one chained program)

audit_program: Decrypt AES-256-CTR (encrypted amount column, host to vram, chained)
workload.commit_programs: two programs submitted together, both in flight: [Filter i64 Gt (amount column, host to host)] and [Encrypt AES-256-CTR (records, host to host)]
workload.record_layout: txn id u64, account u64, amount i64 cents, timestamp u64, merchant u32, currency u16, flags u16, 216 bytes payload
